Kyle Lowry was born on March 25, 1986.
Kyle Terrell Lowry is an American professional basketball player.
Lowry plays for the Philadelphia 76ers of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
Lowry has been named to the All-NBA Third Team once, in 2016.
Lowry won an NBA championship with the Toronto Raptors in 2019.
Lowry is widely regarded as one of the greatest Raptors players of all time.
Lowry played two seasons of college basketball with the Villanova Wildcats.
Lowry was selected by the Memphis Grizzlies in the first round of the 2006 NBA draft, with the 24th overall pick.
Lowry appeared in three seasons with the Memphis Grizzlies before being traded to the Houston Rockets in February 2009.
Lowry spent four seasons with the Houston Rockets.
Lowry was traded to Toronto during the 2012 off-season.
Lowry helped the Raptors reach the playoffs for the first time in six years and win an Atlantic Division title during the 2013–14 season.
Lowry led the Raptors to a then franchise-record of 56 wins in the 2015–16 season.
Lowry was traded to the Miami Heat, where he helped the team reach the 2023 NBA Finals.
Lowry was traded to the Charlotte Hornets via a contract buyout on February 11, 2024.
Lowry signed with the Philadelphia 76ers on February 13, 2024.
Lowry's jersey #1 was retired by the Villanova Wildcats on February 27, 2020.
Lowry suffered a broken wrist against the Cleveland Cavaliers on November 21, 2006.
Lowry underwent season-ending surgery after breaking his wrist in 2006.
Lowry returned for the 2007–08 season and appeared in all 82 games for the Grizzlies.
Lowry competed with Mike Conley Jr. for playing time and the starting point guard position during the 2008–09 season.
Lionel Hollins was named the team's head coach in January 2009, and Lowry was told that the team would devote starter's minutes to Conley.
Lowry played in the post-season for the first time in his career with the Rockets during the 2009–10 season.
Aaron Brooks served as Lowry's backup point guard in the 2009–10 season.
Lowry recorded a career-high 26 points, 10 assists, six rebounds, and five steals in a win over the Dallas Mavericks on December 18, 2009.
The Rockets extended a qualifying offer to Lowry with his contract expiring in June 30, 2010.
Lowry signed an offer sheet with the Cleveland Cavaliers worth $23.5 million over four years on July 13, 2010.
The Rockets quickly matched the offer and retained Lowry.
Lowry started in 71 of the 75 games he played during the 2010–11 season.
On December 3, 2010, Lowry scored a career-high 28 points and matched his career best with 12 assists against the Memphis Grizzlies.
On January 14, 2011, Lowry recorded 17 points and set a career-high 18 assists in a win over the Grizzlies.
Coach Adelman and the Rockets parted ways following the 2010–11 season.
Lowry initially clashed with new head coach Kevin McHale after Adelman's departure.
Lowry appeared in 47 games with 38 starts during the lockout-shortened 66-game 2011–12 season, missing 16 games due to a bacterial infection that required hospitalization.
The Rockets decided they could trade Lowry to improve their salary cap issues and acquire draft picks during the offseason in 2011–12.
On July 11, 2012, Lowry was traded to the Toronto Raptors in exchange for Gary Forbes and a future first round pick.
Lowry averaged over 23 points and seven assists through the first three games of the season with the Raptors.
Lowry was injured during the team's fourth game on November 6, 2012.
Calderón came off the bench behind José Calderón when Lowry was injured in 2012.
Lowry regained the starting position after Calderón was traded to the Memphis Grizzlies on January 30, 2013.
The Raptors finished the season with a 34–48 record and missed the playoffs despite the trade meant to help them return to relevance.
Masai Ujiri was hired as the Raptors' new general manager in May 31, 2013, replacing Bryan Colangelo.
Ujiri believed that Lowry had the potential to be a star but found his reputation more about clashing with coaches and body language than talent.
Lowry received mentorship from Chauncey Billups during the off-season of 2013.
Lowry entered training camp healthy for the first time in several seasons after receiving advice from Ujiri and others.
The Raptors started the 2013–14 season with a 6–12 record until Gay, the team's leading scorer, was traded to the Sacramento Kings.
Following the trade, Lowry and DeMar DeRozan took ownership of the team, knowing they could both be traded if management decided to rebuild rather than compete for a playoff spot.
The Raptors finished the season with a franchise-best 48–34 record, third in the Eastern Conference and first in the Atlantic Division for the second time in franchise history.
Lowry averaged a career-best 17.9 points, 7.4 assists, and 4.7 rebounds during the regular season of the 2013–14 season.
Lowry also averaged 21.1 points, 4.7 assists, and 4.7 rebounds during the playoffs of the 2013–14 season.
Lowry was one of the NBA's most coveted free agents in July 10, 2014, after re-signing with the Raptors to a four-year, $48 million contract.
The Raptors and Lowry continued their strong play into the next season, emerging as top seeds in the Eastern Conference.
Lowry became the team's all-time leader for triple-doubles on November 7, 2014, with a performance against the Washington Wizards.
On December 3, 2014, Lowry scored a career-high 39 points on 13-of-22 shooting in a win against the Utah Jazz.
Lowry was named the Eastern Conference Player of the Month for December 2014 and won Player of the Week during the first week.
On January 5, 2015, Lowry became a first-time All-Star when he was announced as an Eastern Conference starter in the 2015 NBA All-Star Game.
Lowry participated in the 2015 NBA All-Star Weekend Skills Challenge as part of the NBA All-Star Weekend.
On March 16, 2015, Lowry recorded his seventh career triple-double with 20 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists against the Indiana Pacers.
The Raptors finished the 2014–15 season with a franchise-best 49–33 record, fourth in the East and first in the Atlantic.
Lowry averaged 17.8 points, 6.8 assists, and 4.7 rebounds during the regular season of the 2014–15 season but struggled in the playoffs.
Following his disappointing performance in the playoffs, Lowry entered the 2015–16 season with a noticeably slimmer physique.
Lowry explained that he wanted to be prepared for 82 games and a long playoff run during the 2015–16 season.
On November 3, 2015, Lowry scored a game-high 27 points against the Dallas Mavericks as the Raptors started 4–0 for the first time in franchise history.
Lowry passed Alvin Williams for second all-time on the Raptors' assists list on February 1, 2016.
On January 21, 2016, Lowry was named a starter to the Eastern Conference All-Star team for the 2016 NBA All-Star Game.
On February 14, 2016, Lowry finished his second All-Star game with 14 points, 10 assists, 5 rebounds, and 2 steals in the East's 196–173 loss to the West.
On March 21, 2016, Lowry was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week for games played from February 22–28.
On March 30, 2016, Lowry recorded 17 points, 11 assists, and six rebounds in a win over the Atlanta Hawks, helping the Raptors reach 50 wins for the first time in franchise history.
The Raptors finished the regular season with a 56–26 record, good for first in the Atlantic Division for the third consecutive year and second in the Eastern Conference.
Lowry entered the playoffs suffering from bursitis in his shooting elbow.
Lowry shot a mere 32% from the field over the final 10 games of the regular season during the 2015–16 playoffs.
The Raptors defeated the Indiana Pacers in seven games, winning their second playoff series in franchise history and their first since 2001.
In Game 3 of the Raptors' second-round series against the Miami Heat, Lowry broke out of his shooting slump with a 33-point performance on 11-of-19 shooting.
Lowry tied his playoff career high with 36 points on 12-of-27 shooting in a loss to the Heat in Game 6 of the series.
In Game 7 of the series, Lowry scored 35 points on 11-of-20 shooting and helped the Raptors advance to the Eastern Conference Finals for the first time in franchise history.
Lowry was named All-NBA third team honors after his strong season.
On November 28, 2016, Lowry set a franchise record by hitting all six of his three-pointers for a game-high 24 points against the Philadelphia 76ers.
On December 9, 2016, Lowry scored 21 of his then season-high 34 points in the second half against the Boston Celtics.
On December 23, 2016, Lowry set a new season high with 36 points, including 19 in the fourth quarter, to lead the Raptors over the Utah Jazz.
On January 1, 2017, Lowry scored 20 of his season-high 41 points in the fourth quarter against the Los Angeles Lakers.
On February 5, 2017, Lowry recorded his ninth career triple-double with 15 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists against the Brooklyn Nets.
Lowry became the Raptors' franchise leader in three-pointers on February 5, 2017.
On April 5, 2017, Lowry returned from an 18-game absence with a wrist injury and played 42 minutes to help the Raptors overcome a 20-point first-half deficit against the Detroit Pistons.
In Game 2 of the Raptors' second-round playoff series against the Cleveland Cavaliers, Lowry sprained his left ankle in the third quarter and aggravated it while trying to warm up for Game 3.
Lowry was not active for Game 4 due to injury and thus could not assist the Raptors in avoiding a series sweep by the Cavaliers.
Following the playoffs, Lowry declined his $12 million player option for the 2017–18 season and became an unrestricted free agent.
On July 7, 2017, Lowry re-signed with the Raptors to a three-year, $100 million contract.
On October 27, 2017, Lowry recorded his first triple-double of the season and his eighth as a Raptor against the Los Angeles Lakers.
Lowry moved past Andrea Bargnani (6,581 points) into fourth place on Toronto's all-time scoring list with 19 points against the Boston Celtics on November 12, 2017.
On December 23, 2017, Lowry had a career-high 13 rebounds in a win over the Atlanta Hawks.
On January 20, 2018, Lowry scored a season-high 40 points against the Minnesota Timberwolves.
Three days later, on January 23, 2018, Lowry was selected as a reserve for the 2018 NBA All-Star Game.
On February 8, 2018, Lowry passed 11,000 career points against the New York Knicks.
On March 23, 2018, Lowry recorded his 10th triple-double as a Raptor with 25 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds against the Nets.
In Game 2 of the Raptors' first-round playoff series against the Washington Wizards, Lowry had 13 points and a career-playoff high 12 assists.
In Game 6, Lowry scored 24 points in a win over the Wizards to clinch the series for the Raptors.
In the second round, the Raptors were swept by the Cleveland Cavaliers for the second straight year.
Lowry advanced the ball down the court while being guarded by Klay Thompson during Game 2 of the 2019 NBA Finals.
On October 17, 2018, Lowry scored 27 points and had eight assists in a win over the Cleveland Cavaliers to start the season.
On October 26, 2018, Lowry had 20 points and 12 assists in a win over the Dallas Mavericks, recording his 10th consecutive game with double-digit assists.
On October 30, 2018, Lowry scored 20 points and 13 assists against the Philadelphia 76ers, extending his streak of double-digit assist games to a career-best six.
Lowry missed 10 games between December 14 and January 5 due to injury.
On March 3, 2019, Lowry scored a season-high 35 points in a loss against the Detroit Pistons.
On March 8, 2019, Lowry had 13 points, 12 assists, and 11 rebounds in a win over the New Orleans Pelicans.
In Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Finals, Lowry scored 30 points with seven 3-pointers against the Milwaukee Bucks.
On May 2, 2019, Lowry scored 37 points and made eight three-pointers in a win over the Los Angeles Lakers.
On August 6, 2021, Lowry was acquired by the Miami Heat via a sign-and-trade with Goran Dragić and Precious Achiuwa.
On November 6, 2021, Lowry recorded his first triple-double with the Heat against the Utah Jazz with a statline of 20 points, 12 rebounds, and 10 assists.
On December 19, 2021, Kyle Lowry drew the 252nd charge of his career, passing Ersan Ilyasova for most charges drawn in NBA history.
Lowry led the Heat to the top seed in the Eastern Conference with a 53–29 record during the 2021–22 season.
During the 2022 playoffs, Lowry missed multiple games due to a hamstring injury.
On May 27, 2022, Lowry recorded a double-double of 18 points and 10 assists in Game 6 against the Boston Celtics.
In Game 7, the Heat were eliminated by the Celtics with a score of 100–96.
On April 11, 2023, Lowry scored a season-high 33 points against the Atlanta Hawks during the play-in tournament game.
The Heat defeated the Chicago Bulls in a 102–91 win three days later to secure the eighth seed in the playoffs.
In the Finals, the Heat lost in five games to the Denver Nuggets.
On January 23, 2024, Lowry was traded to the Charlotte Hornets alongside a first-round draft pick for Terry Rozier.
Lowry's contract with the Hornets was subsequently bought out on February 11, 2024.
On February 13, 2024, Lowry signed with the Philadelphia 76ers.
Lowry made his 76ers debut on February 13, putting up 11 points, five assists, and four rebounds in a loss to the New York Knicks.
Lowry was a member of the U.S. men's national team that won gold at the 2016 Summer Olympics.
During the 2016 Olympics, Lowry averaged 5 points and 3.3 rebounds per game.
His best scoring performance during the tournament was in the semifinal game against Spain with 9 points.
Lowry earned praise for his defense and leadership during the tournament.
Lowry's playing style is often compared to a pit bull or bulldog due to his toughness, leadership, and instinct for winning plays on the court.
Lowry is considered a strong rebounder for his position and an elite defender.
Lowry holds the Toronto Raptors' franchise record for triple-doubles and most made three-point field goals in a season (2013–14).
Lowry is married to Ayahna Cornish, who played at Saint Joseph's University.
The couple has two sons: Karter (born August 18, 2011) and Kameron (born July 15, 2015).
